title: 2026-11-05_Xbash_Malware_Investigation_and_Response_324
description: Investigate and respond to an Xbash malware infection which combines botnet, ransomware, and coinmining capabilities.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on one of its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests a possible malware infection. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malware's behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the running services on the compromised host and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH: `ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5`
2. List all services: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Identify the suspicious service by looking for unfamiliar service names or unusual descriptions.
4. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is not a standard system service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Determine the network port associated with the suspicious service's communication.
levels.solution:
1. Investigate the suspicious service found in TRAINING_LEVEL 1.
2. Use `systemctl cat <service>` to view the service configuration.
3. Look for the port number in the ExecStart command.
4. The hidden flag is the port number.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service>` to view the service status and recent logs.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified as an argument in the ExecStart command.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is a four-digit number.

levels.title: Suspicious File Discovery
levels.content: Identify the file responsible for collecting system information.
levels.solution:
1. Investigate the suspicious service found in TRAINING_LEVEL 1.
2. Use `systemctl cat <service>` to view the service configuration.
3. Look for the ExecStart command, which specifies the executable file.
4. The hidden flag is the filename.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `ps auxww` to list all running processes and look for the suspicious executable.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: The filename is located in the `/usr/local/bin/` directory.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The filename is a string of characters.
